source_text: τὸ θυσιαστήριον. Ἔδει γὰρ, ἔδει μέτρων αὐτῷ, καὶ λίαν ἀφθονωτάτων. Σχίσαι τε γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτῷ καὶ βοῶν ἔμελλον ἀναφέρεσθαι τμήματα, καὶ ὁλοκαυτώσεις, οἰῶν τε καὶ τράγων ἀναφοραὶ καθιερουμένων Θεῷ. Ταύτῃτοι χαλκῆ καὶ ἐσχάρα καὶ πυρεῖον αὐτῷ, κρεάγραι τε καὶ φιάλαι, καὶ πάντα αὐτοῦ τὰ σκεύη, ὡς ἂν δύναιντο ταῖς κατὰ νόμον θυσίαις, τὴν παρά γε σφῶν αὐτῶν εἰσκομίζοντα χρείαν, ταῖς τοῦ παμφάγου πυρὸς μὴ καταφθείρεσθαι προσβολαῖς. Στεφάνην δὲ καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ ταῖς γωνίαις κέρατα, τῷ τοῦ σχήματος κάλλει προσθήσομεν. Ἄχαρι γὰρ οὐδὲν παρὰ τῷ πανσόφῳ Θεῷ. Πλὴν, ἐκεῖνο πάλιν δὴ φέρε λέγωμεν, ἀκριβῆ τὸν νοῦν ἐπερείδοντες τοῖς ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τεθεσπισμένοις. Θυσιαστήριον προστέταχε ταῖς κατὰ νόμον θυσίαις ἐοικὸς καὶ πρέπον, ἀλλ' οὐδὲν ἐν αὐτῷ χρυσοῦν, καθάπερ ἀμέλει, καταθεῷτό τις ἂν ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ, λυχνίας τε αὖ καὶ τραπέζης, καὶ τῶν ἀμφ' αὐτήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί δὴ οὖν ἄρα καὶ τοῦτό ἐστι; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐ γὰρ δὴ τῆς θείας τε καὶ ἀκηράτου φύσεως τὴν κατὰ πάντων ὑπεροχὴν, καὶ ἀσύγκριτον λαμπρότητα, ὡς ἐν νοήσει λέγω, τὸ χρυσίον εὖ μάλα καταδηλοῦν ἐλέγομεν, ὦ Παλλάδιε; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν, ἀχρύσωτον παντελῶς τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας τὸ θυσιαστήριον, αἴνιγμά που τὸ χρῆμα τιθέντος ἡμῖν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ μάλα σαφῶς, ὅτι Πνεύματος ἁγίου πρόξενος ἥκιστα μὲν ὁ νόμος, τετίμηται δὲ οὐχὶ τοιαύτῃ χάριτι τῆς ἐν τύπῳ λατρείας ἡ δύναμις. Πνεῦμα γὰρ ἦν δουλείας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἡμῖν δὲ τὸ δῶρον ἀπενεμήθη διὰ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναβίωσιν. Ἐνεφύσησε γὰρ, λέγων, «Λάβετε Πνεῦμα ἅγιον.» Τοιγάρτοι καὶ Παῦλος προσεφώνει τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν, «Οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλ' ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας, ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν, Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ.» Ὅτι δὲ τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας ἡ δύναμις τὴν τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος οὐκ ἐπλούτει μέθεξιν, δέδονται δὲ μᾶλλον τοῖς ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένοις, πληροφορήσει λέγων ὁ σοφὸς Ἰωάννης· «Οὔπω γὰρ ἦν Πνεῦμα ἅγιον, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη.» Οὔπω γὰρ ἀνεβίω Χριστός· μονονουχὶ γὰρ τότε κατεχρυσώθη τῷ Πνεύματι, καὶ κοινωνίᾳ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν, ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις. Χρυσοῦ μὲν δὴ δίχα, ταύτῃτοι γενέσθαι προστέταχε τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καθάπερ ἐγῷμαι, τὸν δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ χαλκῷ λόγον, ἐξ οὗ καὶ πεποίητο, παραδραμεῖν, ὡς ἔοικε, τοῖς φιλομαθέσιν οὐκ ἀζήμιον. Ἐκτέκοι γὰρ ἄν τι τῶν ἀναγκαίων ἡ βάσανος, καθάπερ τὸ ὑπό του σοφῶς εἰρημένον, Ἐν παντὶ μεριμνῶντι ἔνεστι περιττόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί οὖν ἂν ἔχοις εἰπεῖν καὶ ἐπὶ τῷδε πάλιν; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄκουε δή· ψήφῳ μὲν γὰρ τῇ ἄνωθεν εἰς ἱερέα καὶ ἡγούμενον τὸν θεσπέσιον Ἀαρὼν κεχειροτονῆσθαί φησι τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερόν. Κορέ γε μὴν καὶ Δαθὰν, καὶ τοῖς ἀμφ' αὐτοὺς, ἡ ἀγρία πληθὺς τῆς ἄνωθεν ψήφου προαλέστατα καταθέοντες, καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. from s.13: five-cubit in breadth and length] the altar. For it needed, it needed measures, and very most ample (ἀφθονωτάτων). For on it were to be brought up both split wood (σχίζαι, printed Σχίσαι) and portions (τμήματα) of oxen, and whole burnt offerings (ὁλοκαυτώσεις), offerings-up (ἀναφοραί) of sheep and goats consecrated (καθιερουμένων) to God. Therefore bronze also its grate (ἐσχάρα) and fire-pan, flesh-hooks and bowls, and all its vessels, so they could, bringing in (εἰσκομίζοντα) their own use (χρεία) to the sacrifices (θυσίαι) according to law, not be destroyed (καταφθείρεσθαι) by the assaults (προσβολαί) of the all-devouring (παμφάγου) fire. Crown and the horns at the corners we will add (προσθήσομεν) to the beauty (κάλλος) of the shape (σχῆμα); for nothing graceless (ἄχαρι) with the all-wise (πάνσοφος) God. But come, let us say that again, pressing (ἐπερείδοντες) an exact mind on things decreed (τεθεσπισμένοις) about each. He ordered (προστέταχε) an altar like and fitting (ἐοικὸς καὶ πρέπον) for the sacrifices according to law, but nothing golden (χρυσοῦν) in it, as surely (ἀμέλει) one would behold (καταθεῷτο) on the ark (κιβωτός), and lampstand and table and the things around it. | PALL.: What then is this? | CYR.: Did we not say, Palladius, that gold (χρυσίον) shows very well the supremacy over all (ὑπεροχή) and incomparable (ἀσύγκριτον) brightness (λαμπρότης) of the divine and undefiled (ἀκηράτου) nature (φύσις), as in thought (ἐν νοήσει), I say? | PALL.: So it is. | CYR.: Look (ἄθρει) then: the altar of worship according to law entirely ungilded (ἀχρύσωτον), God setting the thing as a riddle (αἴνιγμα) for us, and very clearly, that the law is least of all (ἥκιστα) the procurer (πρόξενος) of Holy Spirit, and the power (δύναμις) of the worship in type (ἐν τύπῳ) has not been honored with such grace (χάρις). For there was a spirit of slavery (δουλεία) on Israel; but to us the gift (δῶρον) was allotted (ἀπενεμήθη) through Christ after the return to life (ἀναβίωσις) from the dead. For he breathed in (ἐνεφύσησε), saying: Receive Holy Spirit. Therefore Paul addressed believers: [Rom 8:15] You did not receive a spirit of slavery again to fear, but a spirit of adoption (υἱοθεσία), in which we cry (κράζομεν) Abba, the Father. That the power of the worship according to law did not abound in (ἐπλούτει) participation (μέθεξις) of the Holy Spirit, but [they] have been given (δέδονται) rather to those justified (δεδικαιωμένοις) in faith, wise John [will show] with full assurance (πληροφορήσει) saying: [John 7:39] For not yet was Holy Spirit, because Jesus was not yet glorified (ἐδοξάσθη). For Christ had not yet come back to life (ἀνεβίω); for all but (μονονουχί) then was human nature gilded over (κατεχρυσώθη) by the Spirit and by fellowship (κοινωνία) with him. Without gold, then, for this reason he ordered the altar to be made, as I think; but to run past (παραδραμεῖν) the account (λόγος) about the bronze from which it was made is, it seems, not without loss (οὐκ ἀζήμιον) to lovers of learning (φιλομαθέσιν). For examination (βάσανος) might give birth to (ἐκτέκοι) something necessary, as the thing wisely said by someone: [Prov 14:23 LXX] In everyone taking care (μεριμνῶντι) there is surplus (περιττόν). | PALL.: What could you say on this again? | CYR.: Listen: by the vote (ψῆφος) from above the holy Writing (Γράμμα) says the divine Aaron was elected (κεχειροτονῆσθαι) as priest and leader (ἡγούμενος). Korah and Dathan, and those around them, the wild (ἀγρία) multitude, most rashly (προαλέστατα) running down against (καταθέοντες) the vote from above, and [cont. s.15]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …was the altar. For it needed, yes, it needed measurements, and very generous ones. For on it were to be brought up split logs and portions of oxen, and whole burnt offerings, and offerings of sheep and goats consecrated to God. That is why its grate and firepan were of bronze, and its meat forks and bowls and all its vessels, so that they could render their own service to the sacrifices of the law and not be destroyed by the assaults of the all-devouring fire. The crown and the horns at the corners we will put down to the beauty of its form, for with the all-wise God nothing is graceless. But come, let us make this point once more, fixing our minds closely on what was decreed about each thing. He ordered an altar suited and fitting for the sacrifices of the law, but there is nothing of gold on it, such as one would certainly see on the ark, and again on the lampstand and the table and the things that go with it.
Palladius: And what, then, does this mean?
Cyril: Did we not say, Palladius, that gold very well signifies the supremacy over all things and the incomparable splendor of the divine and pure nature (splendor as the mind conceives it, I mean)?

Cyril: Observe, then, that the altar of the worship under the law is entirely without gold. God sets the matter before us as a kind of riddle, and a very clear one: the law in no way procures the Holy Spirit, and the power of the worship in types has not been honored with such a grace. For a spirit of slavery was upon Israel; but to us the gift was granted through Christ after his return to life from the dead. For he breathed on them, saying, ‘Receive the Holy Spirit’ (John 20:22). That is why Paul also said to those who had believed: ‘For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba, Father”’ (Romans 8:15). And that the power of the worship under the law was not rich in a share of the Holy Spirit, but that this has been given rather to those justified by faith, the wise John will assure us when he says: ‘For the Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus had not yet been glorified’ (John 7:39). For Christ had not yet returned to life; for it was then that human nature was, so to speak, gilded by the Spirit and by fellowship with him. This, then, as I think, is why he ordered the altar to be made without gold. But it seems that to pass over the meaning of the bronze from which it was made would not be without loss for those who love learning. For careful testing may bring forth something needful, as in the saying wisely spoken by someone: ‘In everyone who takes pains there is profit’ (Proverbs 14:23).
Palladius: What, then, could you say about this in turn?

Cyril: Listen, then. Holy Scripture says that the divine Aaron was appointed priest and leader by the decision from above. But Korah and Dathan, and the savage crowd around them, rushing most rashly against the decision from above, and…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, completing s.13. The printed Σχίσαι is read as σχίζαι ('split logs', the wood for the fire), a noun paired by τε…καί with τμήματα; the old English 'they were about to split' does not fit the syntax. 'Grate' (ἐσχάρα) is the bronze grating of Exodus 27:4. 'The law in no way procures the Holy Spirit' renders ἥκιστα πρόξενος ('least of all a procurer'). 'A spirit of slavery was upon Israel' anticipates Romans 8:15, quoted next; not cited separately. 'He breathed on them' follows the usual English of John 20:22, where the Greek also has no object. In Romans 8:15 Cyril's text reads 'Abba, the Father' (ὁ Πατήρ); rendered 'Abba, Father'. In 'has been given rather to those justified by faith' the Greek verb is plural (δέδονται) with no expressed subject; rendered with 'this' (the share of the Spirit). John 7:39 is kept literal, 'the Holy Spirit was not yet', as Cyril quotes it. 'With him' (κοινωνίᾳ τῇ πρὸς αὐτόν) is ambiguous between Christ and the Spirit; kept ambiguous. Cyril introduces Proverbs 14:23 LXX (ἐν παντὶ μεριμνῶντι ἔνεστι περισσόν) as 'wisely said by someone'; the Greek of the LXX differs from the Hebrew ('In all toil there is profit'), so it is translated from his wording but cited. Aaron's appointment 'by the decision from above' may refer to Exodus 28:1 or to the budding rod of Numbers 17; left uncited as a general reference. The section ends mid-sentence at the PG column break.

Gold comparison clause made unambiguous: 'such as one would certainly see on the ark ...'
